   `e120`'s pre-registration derived a seed-to-seed correlation from the forgetting's and the accuracy's sd's —
   **naming its own formula, `sd_forgetting = sd_accuracy·√(2(1−ρ))`** — and reported **ρ ≈ 0.14**. On the
   paragraph's own rounded input that formula gives **0.246** and on the artifacts' exact values
   (**0.01963** and **0.02215**, both from `runs/e119_r128_test480.json`) it gives **0.364**; the `≈ 0.018` it
   used was itself a slight understatement of 0.01963, which is where part of the drift entered. **The
   2000-iteration value in the same pair is right** (0.062 against a reported 0.06), so this was one wrong
   number and not a wrong method — and **the correction strengthens the mechanism rather than weakening it**:
   the drop is **0.364 → 0.062**, a factor of six against the 2.5 the wrong number implied. A third reading
   explains both: **at test 48 the same propagation gives ρ = −0.014**, so the two accuracies are uncorrelated
   across seeds when the test set is coarse and correlated once its sampling noise is removed, which is the
   ordering the mechanism predicts and which was invisible while one of the three values was wrong. **All four
   of this project's audits were green on it** — `e97` reads artifact existence, `e105` table closure, `e126`
   counts, `e127` the programme table — because it is a sentence (`docs/findings/2026-09-24-rule-34-had-a-second-instance.md`).
   **What the rule cannot catch, stated because a rule that looks total is dangerous: it applies only where the
   text names its own formula.** `e128`'s `2.6×` named none and was caught by recomputing anyway; a claim whose
   model the reader cannot reconstruct from the sentence is invisible to this check, and there the only defence
   is that **a number quoted beside its input is worth more than a number quoted alone**.

   **And the rule is now a check rather than a habit.** Its three instances are known: §4.2's `2.6×` (**wrong**,
   the formula gives **2.07** from the 85% in the same sentence), `e120`'s `ρ ≈ 0.14` (**wrong**, **0.364**), and
   `side`'s implied draw sd **1.028e-3** (**correct** to 0.3%) — **two defects in three hand-checks, on numbers
   the paper cites**, which is the case for code. `e132` checks the corpus's two formula families by arithmetic
   (`Y = 1/sqrt(0.1f + 1 − f)` for a removable share against a tenfold test set, and `d = s·sqrt((A/B)² − 1)` for
   a σ reduction against a stated sem), **enumerates** the derivation-bearing paragraphs whose formula is not
   named in the sentence, and prints both denominators — because **a zero with no denominator is not a check**.
   The corpus yields **one live derivation and it passes**; 9 paragraphs are enumerated-unchecked and 4 are
   skipped as already-corrected quotations, the second of which is **also an evasion route** and is why the skip
   count is printed. **Three ways prose defeated the checker** are worth keeping, because each is a way a checker
   becomes worse than nothing: it **read lines rather than sentences**, so the one derivation that wraps across
   two lines was invisible and **silence looked like having no subject**; it reported three **already-corrected
   quotations** as defects, since the convention is to correct in a `>` blockquote *after* the wrong sentence; and
   then the exclusion was **too wide** — a marker five paragraphs later, about a different figure, silently
   skipped a **correct** derivation. **And the test written for it had the same class of error**: it asserted
   `share_sd_fall(0.85) = 2.074` where the formula gives **2.063**, because 2.074 is what the *measured* 0.8528
   gives — the round number in the prose and the value in the artifact are two numbers and the formula uses one
   (`docs/findings/2026-09-24-rule-34-is-now-a-check.md`).

35. **"A factor below chance" is a unit if and only if its numerator is an absolute loss.** `ln 4` divided
   by a **fraction of chance** is a different quantity from `ln 4` divided by a **loss in nats**, and the two
   differ by exactly `ln 4 = 1.386`. Three documents carried the wrong one — `e124`'s, `e130`'s and `e131`'s
   "worst chord is 11.07x / 3.14x / 7.24x below chance" — because the measured quantity is
   `barrier / ln 4` (a fraction) and it was divided into `ln 4` a second time. **The correct figures are
   7.99x, 2.26x and 5.22x**, or better, the fractions they come from: **12.52%, 44.19% and 19.15% of chance**.
   **This is `e123`'s cross-unit defect in a second costume** — there it was an sd in nats divided by an sd in
   accuracy, here it is a dimensionless ratio divided into a loss — and the repair is the same one: **state both
   numbers, the fraction and then the factor beside it**, because a sentence that writes *"12.52% of chance,
   7.99x below it"* cannot contain this error while one that writes *"a factor of 11.07 below chance"* can.
   Two instances in the corpus are correct and show what the convention costs: the `e124` registration wrote
   *"25% of chance is four times below that scale"* (the fraction first), and `e122`'s "26x below chance" comes
   from an absolute loss of 0.05399 nats, where the division is the right one. **The check is that every
   "factor below" figure must sit beside the fraction or the loss it was divided from**
   (`docs/findings/2026-09-24-the-barrier-orders-like-the-bodys-load.md`).

   **Extended 2026-09-24 by `e134`, which found the same error a third time and in a form that reorders a
   registered prediction: an effect against a *varying* baseline.** The frozen-bias effect was registered as an
   ordering of the **fraction** of the naive forgetting removed, and at read-out 128 that fraction is **89%**
   against read-out 32's **70%** — so the registered ordering **fails** — while the **absolute** differences order
   the other way (**0.0523 > 0.0331**), matching the load-bearing gap. The comparators' levels differ by a factor
   of **2.0** and the effects by only **1.6×**, so dividing by them reorders what it was meant to rank. **And the
   same fire found it again in a spread**: the per-repeat sd falls **2.69×** at read-out 32 and **3.04×** at 128,
   while the *relative* sd moves the opposite way — **74% → 91%** at 32 and **88% → 275%** at 128, where removing
   the channel collapsed the mean to 0.0039 and left almost all noise. **The general form, and it covers all three
   of this session's instances: a registered ordering must name its unit, and every results sentence should carry
   both numbers wherever the normaliser varies across the configurations being compared** — a fixed reference (a
   chance level) wants fraction and factor, a varying baseline wants absolute and fraction, and a spread wants
   absolute and relative. In this benchmark the normalisers vary by 2× across read-outs and by ∞ within one, which
   is why all three cases happened here and not elsewhere
   (`docs/findings/2026-09-24-the-bias-effect-is-not-a-read-out-32-artefact.md`).

36. **An instrument assembled from *part* of the object reports a null about the part it read, and a
   manipulation shows that where a correlation cannot.** The first-order interference term is
   `<grad_j(theta_final), theta_final - theta_after_j>` — built from **`theta` alone** — and `e108` found it
   unable to order the forgetting across configurations, which the project recorded for five fires as *"the term
   is dominated by two magnitudes that are themselves monotone in the read-out"*. **Both accounts are true and
   the second one explains the first**: the body is **two** parameter sets, `e125` measured that the 800 offsets
   carry **70%** of this configuration's forgetting, and `e137` that the penalty's effect on `theta` is matched by
   an **opposite movement** in them — so a term reading `theta` is evaluated over the half of the body where most
   of the damage is not, and **its failure to order the effect is not evidence about the effect**. The measurement
   that settles it is a **manipulation**: at forty paired seeds diagonal EWC cuts the `theta`-only term by **98%**
   (`+0.2336 → +0.0052`, **10.34σ**) with the cosine down 96% (**14.41σ**) and the displacement down 25%
   (**28.25σ**), while **the forgetting moves 1.21σ**. **A quantity that can be moved forty-five-fold by an
   intervention, with the effect it exists to predict not moving, is not the effect's carrier** — and the
   contrast with a correlation is the point: a correlation across configurations can be confounded by anything
   monotone along the axis being varied, which is exactly what this project's read-out axis is, while a 45-fold
   manipulation cannot be. **So when a quantity is assembled from a subset of a model's parameters, its null is a
   null about that subset until the subset's share of the effect is measured** — and the repair is to extend the
   instrument and keep the old form beside the new one, which is what `whole_body_grad` and the `interference`
   block's `theta_only_cumulative` / `bias_only_cumulative` split do, so that five fires of record stay readable
   rather than being overwritten
   (`docs/findings/2026-09-24-the-interference-instrument-is-channel-blind.md`).
   **(*Measured the same day, and the repair works.*)** The extended instrument was run: the whole-body
   first-order term is **+0.4266 → +0.3257**, ratio **0.763** at **1.39σ**, against the θ-only form's 0.022 at
   **10.34σ** — and the **bias's own share is 45%** of the naive arm's whole-body term, *growing* 66% under the
   penalty (**1.82σ**) so that the θ-only form's share of the instrument collapses **98% → 2%** between the arms.
   **And across three arms whose effect differs by 4.84σ the extended form orders the forgetting while the old
   one does not**: whole body **0.4266 → 0.3257 → 0.1831** (the last at ratio **0.429, 4.21σ**) against
   forgetting 0.0750 → 0.0654 → 0.0292, while the θ-only form (0.2336 → **0.0052** → 0.0238) is **lowest in
   the arm whose forgetting is highest of the three penalties**. **So a part-assembled instrument's null is not
   only a null about the part — the whole-body form is the one that carries the effect, which makes the
   original account *repaired* rather than discarded.** **And the same fire produced the companion defect one
   step over**: ordering the penalty arms on this configuration by the **bias's cumulative path** gives
   **3.4452 → +0.0292**, **3.6835 → +0.0396**, **4.2190 → +0.0352**, **4.2819 → +0.0654**, **5.4367 → +0.0810**,
   **6.2313 → +0.0846** — **Spearman +0.943 with exactly one inversion, and that inversion unresolved at 0.69σ**
   — while **within each knob it is perfect** (+1.000 over the four λ arms, +1.000 over the three anchoring arms).
   **So a three-point ordering along a single intervention is a co-movement, not a carrier**, and the test of
   whether a quantity carries an effect is a **second, independent knob** — the same reason a correlation along a
   read-out axis is confounded by everything else that axis moves, arriving here on an *intervention* axis rather
   than on a configuration axis. **And the test cuts both ways**: the first reading of this table was three arms
   and the second was four, and *both* were too strong — the six-arm version is neither the clean ordering the
   first claimed nor the breakage the second reported
   (`docs/findings/2026-09-24-the-lambda-sweeps-floor-is-where-the-effect-is.md`).

37. **A registered threshold on a statistic needs that statistic's own uncertainty, or it is a coin-flip
    dressed as a bar.** `e142` registered "raising the input overlap raises the forgetting, resolved at
    **≥ 3σ**" and measured **2.9876σ**: a 3.00σ bar needs an effect of **0.03190** and the effect is
    **0.03177**, so the prediction **misses by 0.01σ** — while the sign test on the same forty pairs gives
    **29/40 positive, two-sided p = 0.0064**, and the falsifier (within 2σ) plainly does not fire. **The bar was
    soft and the measurement landed on it**: a sem estimated from forty pairs carries a relative uncertainty of
    about **11%**, so the same data are consistent with 2.7σ or 3.4σ and *the registered form of the prediction
    cannot distinguish "met" from "missed" at that resolution*. **The fix is not a lower bar** — it is that a
    threshold has to be either far enough from the estimate to be decidable at the sample size, or the
    registration has to say which of the several available forms (paired σ, sign test, effect ratio) is the one
    that decides, **before** the number is known. This is rule 30's demand — *a cost computed from an sd needs
    the same evidential standard as the effect* — arriving on the **threshold** rather than on the cost
    (`docs/findings/2026-09-24-at-the-registration-s-resolution-limit.md`). **And the same day produced the
    defect one level up, from the other direction: the *metric* is part of the statistic too.** `e141` registered
    its P2 as *"λ = 3e-2 worse than λ = 3e-3 at ≥2σ"* with the quantity named as **mean forgetting** — the
    accuracy-valued one — and measured **1.60σ**; **the same forty pairs in the same artifact give 4.24σ on the
    loss-valued forgetting**, a quantity the project was already recording, and the two metrics rank those seeds
    at **+0.51 to +0.71 within each of five arms**, so they are not in conflict — they differ on whether a 0.016
    effect is resolvable at forty pairs. **So a registration has to name the metric as well as the form**, and
    this is the reason: **naming the contrast without naming the quantity chooses the bar and the outcome
    together.** The verdict stands as registered — `e141`'s P2 **fails** — while the question it asked is answered
    *yes* by another quantity in the same file
    (`docs/findings/2026-09-24-the-metric-decides-the-threshold.md`).

38. **A conclusion drawn from the endpoint of a range is a statement about the range.** Three instances, and the
    repair is the same each time. **(a)** The λ sweeps stopped at **0.003** and the project recorded *"0.003 is the
    only useful setting"* — and λ = **3e-4**, five times below every point ever tried, **wins on both metrics**
    (4.27σ over `naive` with accuracy *not* worse, where 3e-3 at forty is 1.21σ and costs 2.69σ of accuracy), so
    the sentence was about a grid whose **floor was the optimum it found**. **(b)** A **cost** range put the rung
    question at 0.9–12 h and its upper end was the one rung *still finishing*, so the range made the question look
    roughly four times cheaper at its low end than the measurements supported. **(c)** The **read-out** axis has an
    **interior minimum** which only appeared when the axis was extended past the sizes the first sweeps used.
    **So a sweep's endpoints are part of its result**: when the optimum sits at or beyond one, the licensed
    sentence is *"the best point measured"*, and the repair is either to extend the range or to say plainly that
    the optimum is **unbracketed** — which is what today's λ result says from the other side, since an interior
    optimum found afterwards means the first sweep's endpoints were **both** wrong
    (`docs/findings/2026-09-24-the-lambda-sweeps-floor-is-where-the-effect-is.md`,
    `docs/findings/2026-09-23-the-cost-range-excluded-the-expensive-rung.md`,
    `docs/findings/2026-09-23-the-read-out-axis-has-an-interior-minimum.md`).

39. **A registered prediction must name the *arm* it is measured on, because a prediction about a quantity the
    manipulated variable cannot reach is not a prediction but a guaranteed outcome.** `e146` registered *"the
    uncovered share falls below 70% when λ falls"* — and the uncovered share is **the share of the `naive` arm's
    forgetting that freezing the offsets removes**, while `naive` builds no Fisher and **cannot read `--lam`**. The
    artifact came back **bit-identical to its comparator** (forty replicates, forgetting and accuracy and drift,
    with `lam` and `fisher_batches` both differing in `config`) — **and that is the tell**: an exact match where a
    difference was predicted means the prediction was fixed before the data, not that the effect is absent. **The
    repair is to put the control on the arm that carries the effect**, which is what `e147` does (`--frozen-bias
    --methods ewc`, where the penalty *is* the manipulated thing). **And the same shape has a benign twin worth
    keeping apart from it**: `e140`'s C0b probe asked whether four unread settings reach an arm and was registered
    as a **control that must hold**, so its bit-identical outcome was the prediction; **the defect is not "a
    setting the code does not read" but "a prediction about a quantity the manipulation cannot move"**
    (`docs/findings/2026-09-24-the-third-point-could-not-exist.md`,
    `docs/findings/2026-09-24-the-frozen-body-control-is-in-no-artifact.md`).

40. **An ordering, frontier or dominance claim is made of point estimates until its own pairwise resolutions are
    printed beside it — and the two must not appear in one sentence without the grade.** `e152` places nine arms in
    a two-axis plane and asks which are dominated; **the first draft of its finding said *"`replay` dominates all
    eight constrained arms and every one of those dominances is resolved on both axes"*, and the printed grades say
    seven of the eight** (the eighth, over `frozen+ewc`, is resolved on one axis — newest 8.33σ, forgetting 1.28σ)
    **while three pairs are point estimates only** (`anchored 1.0` by `anchored 33.2`, at 0.88σ and 0.79σ). **So a
    dominance is two claims, not one**: that one arm is no worse on both axes (arithmetic, always checkable) and
    that the difference would survive another draw of seeds (a resolution, which the plane does not have by
    construction). The rule is the ordering-side twin of rule 37's *"a threshold needs its own uncertainty"*, and
    it is not idle: **a partial order drawn from point estimates is a weaker object than the same order resolved,
    and this project's whole C2b line has now had three findings whose wording was stronger than their
    resolutions** (`docs/findings/2026-09-24-the-lambda-optimum-is-a-dominance-boundary.md`,
    `docs/findings/2026-09-24-the-aggregate-hides-the-diagonal-and-the-last-task-pays.md`).

41. **A bar must be placed between the competing predictions, not at a round number — and when two readings
    predict values inside each other's 2σ windows, the registration must say so *before* the run.** Four
    registrations today ended in their own middle rather than at a bar, and in each case the bar was a round
    number chosen without asking what the alternatives predicted: `e141`'s P2 measured **+0.0156 ± 0.0098 =
    1.60σ** against a 2σ bar; `e142`'s P1 measured **+0.03177** against a 3σ bar needing **+0.03190**, a miss of
    **0.012σ**; `e148`'s P2 measured **−0.0201 ± 0.0124 = 1.62σ** *in the falsifier's direction* against a 2σ
    bar; and `e150`'s P1 landed at **+0.0190** between its own P1 bar (**+0.0149**) and its falsifier bar
    (**+0.0318**). **A bar at the noise scale does not test a hypothesis, it tests the seeds.** The repair has
    two halves, and `e150`'s registration is the worked example of the good one: **write down what each competing
    reading predicts** — *the pair is the unit → +0.0069, the family scales it → +0.0314, the penalty is
    saturated → +0.0398* — then place the bars at the edges of the interval those predictions span, **naming the
    middle as an outcome rather than as a failure**. And when two readings' predictions fall inside each other's
    2σ windows, **the registration should say the design cannot separate them** and either change the design or
    record what the run *can* decide. The measurable form of the same defect is the **relative** uncertainty of a
    sem at n = 40, which `e142` put at about **11%**: any bar within ~10% of the predicted effect is not decidable
    at that n, and the number belongs in the finding as a bound
    (`docs/findings/2026-09-24-at-the-registration-s-resolution-limit.md`,
    `docs/findings/2026-09-24-the-metric-decides-the-threshold.md`,
    `docs/findings/2026-09-24-replays-margin-tracks-the-baselines-forgetting.md`,
    `docs/findings/2026-09-24-the-penalty-is-family-dependent-in-stability-and-blind-in-cost.md`).

42. **A registration whose predicted effect would need more seeds than the project will run is a bound, not a bar —
    and the price is computable before the run.** Rule 41 said *place the bar between the competing predictions
    rather than at a round number*; `e157` adds the arithmetic that turns it from a style rule into a budget one.
    From the forty paired seeds already on disk, the seeds a contrast needs for 3σ at its **measured** effect are:
    **4 for `replay − naive` (plastic, 9.35σ), 10–11 for the frozen arm's `ewc`/`replay` at 5.85–5.89σ, 16 for the
    wiring diagonal, 83 for the biology's own contrast in the plastic arm, 169 for the frozen λ step, 246 for the
    plastic diagonal, 372 for the biology in the frozen arm, and 1,237–12,567 for the biology on the shared-input
    family** — where the last three are **333, 1,489 and 50,269 at *half* the measured effect**, which is what a
    larger study would tend to find. **The median is 83 at the measured effect and 333 at half of it**, so *the
    line's forty seeds sit at the median requirement*, which is exactly why four registrations this session landed
    in their own middle (1.60σ, 2.99σ, 1.62σ and a mid-zone landing — all of them effects whose n(3σ) is 83 to
    1,237). **The rule's form is therefore: quote the prediction, quote what each reading predicts, and quote the
    seeds the test would need; if that number is beyond what the queue will pay, write the claim as a bound and say
    which bound** (`docs/findings/2026-09-24-what-each-live-contrast-costs-in-seeds.md`).

43. **A rank statistic over cells is uninterpretable unless the cells' own values are resolved — print the count
    resolved from zero and the leave-one-out range beside the coefficient.** This is rule 40's defect one level
    down: 40 requires a dominance claim to carry its *pairwise* resolutions, and this requires a rank correlation
    to carry its *inputs'* resolutions. `e156` asked two forms of the same question of the same ten cells with the
    same statistic: the **first-order** whole-body term gives **ρ = +0.927** over cells whose medians sit **11.8σ**
    from zero, and the **second-order** one gives **+0.564** over cells whose median is **1.21σ**, with **only 2 of
    10 resolved at all** (and the cell carrying most of the correlation is the worst measured, `quad = 5.43` at
    1.44σ against its own sem of 3.78). **Removing any single cell moves the second-order ρ between +0.400 and
    +0.867 and the first-order one between +0.900 and +0.950** — so the two rows differ in whether their inputs
    are measurements, not in how well they order. **The near-miss is why the rule exists**: the first draft of that
    finding read *"the second-order term orders the cells at +0.564, weaker than the first-order forms"*, which is
    a sentence about curvature and was really a sentence about a standard error
    (`docs/findings/2026-09-24-the-second-order-term-at-ten-cells.md`).

44. **A C0 identity claim — and any claim that a configuration has been *executed twice* — must be checked against
    the two artifacts' `config` fields, not against a command as paraphrased in a registration.** `e153`'s row named
    `--methods` and `--repeats` and not `--lam`, the launch then used the paraphrase, and the runner's default is
    `lam = 1.0`: **so the artifact ran at 333× the penalty strength of the run it was registered to reproduce, and
    the C0a claim was false when it was written rather than discovered to be false.** Everything followed from that
    one field — the three arms that "failed" are the three that read `lam`, `naive` and `replay` were bit-identical
    because they do not, and the magnitude was a stronger penalty — and **three artifacts were written on the
    mistaken premise before a single `config` comparison refuted it** (`e103` reads exactly that field for its
    signatures, so the check was one command away the whole time). **The corollary is rule 39's benign twin read
    from the other side**: two runs with different configs are still bit-identical on every arm that cannot read the
    difference, so **bit-identity is evidence about which fields a method reads and not evidence that the
    configurations are the same** — which is why `e146`'s bit-identical artifact was a tell about a mistaken
    prediction rather than a reproduction (`docs/findings/2026-09-24-the-penalty-arms-were-never-non-reproducible.md`).

45. **Two executions of one configuration that disagree are not "noise" by default: noise moves a *repeated* pair
    apart, so when two later executions agree with each other and disagree with an earlier one, the object of the
    claim is an *epoch* — and the first thing to write down is which of the three cases the movement is in, because
    they license different sentences.** A movement inside **one recorded environment** is a reproducibility failure;
    a movement between **two recorded environments** has a named cause (`e77`'s thread knob); a movement in a run
    with **no recorded environment** is unattributable, and the number must carry that word. `e163` tabulated the
    corpus's ten repeated configurations and the three cases are **33 runs, 0 runs and 7 runs**: the floor is
    **exactly 0.0000** where the environment is recorded (**10 of 18 arm-comparisons bit-identical**), the empty
    middle row means `e103`'s environment split has **never fired on real data**, and the seven that moved are
    **exactly the seven written before the field existed** — so the classification is total and is an
    *identification*, not an experiment. **Inside the one group with repeats on both sides of the change, the
    movement is what an epoch looks like and not what noise looks like**: `e101_rate_fb8` (15:34) differs from both
    later runs on `ewc-block`, `ewc-block-rand` and `replay` and on nothing else, the two later runs agree on all
    five arms and all five seeds (not a re-dump — `timing_s` differs, **968.766 s against 969.858 s**), the thread
    knob is excluded because it moves `naive` and `naive` did not move, no commit touching `experiments/` or `clfly/`
    falls in the window, and in the *other* configuration the same three arms move with `replay` taking **exactly
    the same two values** (0.033333 and 0.050000) against 8 Fisher batches and 128 — a change in the replay path,
    which `e160` derives as not reading that field. **So the rule's operative half is provenance**: `config` plus
    `environment` was short by one dimension (the code revision), and no artifact in this corpus records one, which
    is why an afternoon's worth of working-tree state is now unrecoverable
    (`docs/findings/2026-09-24-the-floor-is-zero-and-the-one-move-is-an-epoch.md`).

46. **A contrast that uses a matched-random control arm across two artifacts must identify the draw on **both**
    sides — by printing `partition_draw.fingerprint_sha1` or by reconstructing it from the `config` fields that
    determine it — and must report the between-draw spread measured **on that same family** as the size of the
    term being ruled out.** Rule 10 has said since it was written that the control is a population and one draw is
    one sample, and `partition_draw` is a **top-level** field, so `e103`'s identity check cannot see it: **two
    artifacts whose draws differ are the same configuration by every check this corpus applies.** `e168` counted
    the exposure — **38 artifacts run a `*-rand` arm, 7 record the draw, 31 cannot say which sample they used**,
    and of the 703 pairs sharing such an arm **5 are licensed by two matching fingerprints, 16 are known to be
    *different* samples, 217 have one side only and 465 have neither** — and then measured the quantity at stake on
    the only two pairs that isolate it, which are `e144`'s and `e140`'s own draw 1 against draw 2: **two samples of
    one control differ by 0.0138 on forgetting and 0.0068 on the newest task at forty seeds and neither difference
    resolves**, and the same control is **2.5× noisier on the wiring family than on the base family**, so a spread
    may not be lent between families. **Applied to `e162`'s block-rand column, whose pair has the field on one side
    only (`e144` has none, `e153` records `000b42be6ba2`), the rule was satisfied by reconstruction rather than by
    reading**: the pre-flag call site seeds the draw with `args.seed0`, the flag defaults to the same value, and
    rebuilding the draw from the recorded fields **reproduces all three recorded fingerprints exactly**, so the two
    sides are one sample — had they not been, the forgetting column (0.0112 at 1.09σ) would have been under the
    draw and the newest-task column (0.0219 at 4.19σ) would have been 3.2× it. **And only the random arm is ever
    exposed**: `ewc-block`'s partition comes from `circ.labels[basis]` with no seed in it at all (`docs/findings/2026-09-24-the-random-control-is-a-sample-and-31-of-38-artifacts-do-not-say-which.md`).

47. **An artifact's timestamp dates the *end* of its run, so a long run's code epoch is set by its start — and the
    timestamp can therefore sit on the wrong side of a commit the run never contained.** This is the third way
    today that `e103`'s code-epoch reading can be right and the sentence built on it wrong: the epoch is read from a
    `config` **keyset**, which the runner dumps from the parser it loaded, so it describes the *start*, while the
    file's mtime describes the *finish* and `timing_s` is the difference between them. **`e144` is the worked
    example and it was decisive**: its `timing_s` is **15474 s (4.30 h)**, so its process began around 09:57 on
    09-24 — **twenty-four minutes before `5a0f06e` added `--partition-seed` at 10:21** — which is why an artifact
    written *after* that commit has no `partition_seed` in its `config` and why its matched-random draw had to be
    reconstructed rather than read. For `e163`'s sixteen-minute fb8 runs the same error is seconds, so the rule is
    not that timestamps are useless but that **a run's duration has to be subtracted before an artifact is dated
    against a commit.** **And the rule has a check and a number now** (`e169`): `e103`'s premise that a parser
    only gains flags makes a config **keyset** a monotone clock, so in every strictly-nested keyset pair the
    smaller one must come first — and over **5,263 such pairs** among the 129 run artifacts with a duration,
    **write time orders 3 of them wrongly and start time orders 0**, with every violation involving a run of four
    hours or more (the two longest in the corpus, 5.34 h and 4.30 h, against a median of 16 min). `e144`'s epoch is
    now fixed in two independent directions — its **29-key** config, which cannot exist after the flag, and its
    **start** time 21 minutes before the commit, where only its write time disagrees — and the reconstruction that
    saved `e162`'s block-rand column rests on that dating (`e169`; `docs/findings/2026-09-25-the-timestamp-is-a-
    correct-clock-for-short-runs-and-fails-on-the-longest-ones.md`).

48. **An artifact that does not say what it was measured in is not evidence about a field — and refusing such
    pairs is sound, with a cost that can be named: it is exactly the set of verdicts whose only support was an
    unattributable pair.** `e160`'s readership table is a join over `config`, and the environment is not in `config`,
    so a pair whose arms moved because the *machine* differed was being counted as evidence about a field: **the two
    `fisher_batches` conflicts the table reported for two days had different causes that look identical from a
    `config` alone** — for `naive` the `_omp1`/`_omp4` **thread** difference, for `replay` the `e101`→`e102` **code
    epoch** — and both are unfalsifiable from either field because **both sides of those pairs are unrecorded**.
    **The rule's three parts are each a defect found one level down from the last**: an absent key and a stored
    `None`/`False` are the same statement (comparing them as values made a **schema epoch** look like an intervention
    and turned `frozen_bias × naive` CONFLICTING); the environment is a field **minus its timing**, since the first
    attempt at this keyed on the whole block and lost `lam`'s clean verdict because two runs of one command never
    share a calibration; and an unrecorded environment is neither equal nor different but **unusable**. **Measured**: the
    table has **no conflict about a field left** (all five CONFLICTING cells are the `environment:unrecorded` marker,
    and the 97 artifacts that record an environment give **zero**), **23 cells** are decided only by the sharper
    rule and now read `possibly read` (each an assumption that an unrecorded environment was the default), and
    **exactly 1 goes the other way, which is the rule earning its keep**: `fisher_batches × naive` was CONFLICTING
    and is now **`unread` on two 40-replicate recorded-environment pairs** (`docs/findings/2026-09-25-the-readership-table-classifies-its-own-conflicts.md`).

49. **A cost quoted in a registration is an *extrapolation* until the run lands: write it as an estimate, say what it
    scales from, and record the actual beside it — because the scaling assumption is usually the circuit's size and that
    is usually wrong.** `e181` is the worked example and it took twenty minutes to find: `e79`'s **8305 s** at cs = 1500 was
    scaled down to cs = 300 and the row said **"minutes"**, and at **25 minutes in the run was still going** — so the analytic
    line's cost does not fall with the circuit the way the extrapolation assumed, and `e79`'s `timing` block holds a **single
    total** with nothing to decompose, so the scaling never had support. **The rule is not "measure everything"**: it is that a
    number in a registration is a prediction like any other and has to be *labelled* as one, because a prediction that reads as a
    measurement is exactly the failure this project's audits exist to catch — and rule 42 already says the same thing about the
    seed budget a test needs, which is another quantity written before the run and read afterwards
    (`docs/research_plan.md`'s `e181` row, and `docs/findings/2026-09-25-the-ladders-plateau-is-circuit-specific.md`).

50. **An audit whose subject is "does document A carry number N" is SILENCED BY ITS OWN WRITE-UP: freeze the flagged set
    at the time of the run, because the finding that reports a flag quotes the number and the number then appears in the
    corpus the audit reads.** Measured twice in one session on two instruments. `e184`'s classes: the single file with no
    citation of any kind was `runs/e43_e5_replication.json`, and the finding that reported it **cited it**, so the count
    printed afterwards is 0 where that finding's table says 1. `e192` on the plan: the two numbers no finding carried were
    `1.5e-9` (an agreement between two `replay` arms computed in the row) and `40.5` (a heartbeat's projection), and after
    the finding that reports them was written, the same run reports **0 unsupported** — not because the class was resolved
    but because the report now contains both numbers. **So the flagged set is evidence only in the run that produced it**
    (`--json-out` exists for this reason), and a re-run after the write-up measures the write-up. This is rule 49's shape in
    the audit direction: a quantity that is read after the thing it describes has changed is not the quantity that was
    measured (`docs/findings/2026-09-25-the-plans-citations-localise-rows-not-numbers.md` section 4).

51. **A read's threshold is QUOTED from the registration's sentence, not paraphrased from its motivation — and every
    number a registration quotes is recomputed from the artifact that carries it, with the registration's value printed
    beside the artifact's rather than replacing it.** `e191` has now mis-stated the *same* registration twice, and both
    times in the first print: it applied P1's bar at every level although the sentence is written for achieved 0.3333
    (fixed earlier today), and it applied `prog >= 0.6 * analytic` although both carriers of P2 — the registration
    finding's section 4 and the plan's own row — say the **network's** near rise should be ">= 60% complete" there. The
    applied bar is 60% of the analytic line's 76.4%, i.e. **45.9%, fourteen points looser**, and the case that
    separates them (a 50% measurement) is the case the tests now pin. The same audit found the registration quoting
    **80%** where the arithmetic in its own parenthetical gives **76%** and `e7` gives **76.4%**, with a corpus grep
    finding `80%` in exactly one place: that sentence. So: quote the sentence into the code's comment and compare it
    word by word — "60% complete" is a fraction of the thing the subject names, and "60% of X" is not; and print the
    registration's number beside the artifact's instead of correcting it, because a pre-registration is the only record
    of what was predicted and editing it in place destroys the evidence (rule 50's corollary).
    (`docs/findings/2026-09-25-p2s-bar-is-60-percent-and-the-read-applied-46.md`)

52. **A guard written for one pairing is not a guard for the next — and a reader that drops a row SILENTLY is a reader
    whose absences cannot be read.** `e191` guarded its *anchor* pairing against a replicate-count mismatch, in a
    comment that names the class, and did not guard the *baseline* pairing four lines above: a level with 4 replicates
    against the live 40 raised `operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (4,) (40,)` inside `paired`, which
    **aborts the whole read** and takes the levels that were fine with it. A crash is worse than a refusal. `e188`'s
    mirror defect is the other direction: `if a["n"] != b["n"]: continue` made the arm **vanish with no trace**, and a
    missing row reads as "the artifact does not carry this arm", which is a different fact. Both now refuse with the
    counts named, and **both reports print the refusals** — without that a level prints its heading and no arms, which
    is the same refusal-looks-like-an-answer shape as the misspelled artifact names (`overlap{25,50,75}` where the
    launch wrote `025`/`050`/`075`, which made two tests pass while asserting that levels which exist were "not
    written yet"). **The pre-flight is the instrument that finds this class**: a *payload* for a registered reader,
    built before its artifact, exercising the whole path — because every existing test built its payload with a
    matching count, and no audit reads the code path between a claim and an artifact.
    (`docs/findings/2026-09-25-a-pre-flight-found-a-crash-where-a-refusal-belongs.md`)

53. **Every RNG draw a run makes is a sample of that run's configuration, so a claim measured on one draw is
    conditional on it and the corpus must record WHICH draw — the read-out subset, the matched-random partition and
    the overlap suite's SUPPORTS are three separate draws with three separate flags.** Rule 10 says the control is a
    population and one draw is one sample; today extended that to the substrate. Two support draws, on identical
    configurations and identical 40 seeds, differ by **3.34σ on `learned (older)` at overlap 0.0** and by **4.40σ /
    6.59σ / 4.95σ on that quantity, the newest task and the adjacent-pair term at achieved 0.3333** — and **six of
    the axis's claims failed to replicate across them**, including the day's 8.10σ headline (which **reversed sign**)
    and the registered P1 of the original pre-registration (NOT met on draw 0, MET at 4.70σ on draw 1). **`--support-seed`
    did not exist until today**, so **127 of the 130 artifacts whose supports are a live draw cannot say which draw
    they used (2.3% identified)**; `e198`'s census counts **80 of 144** for the read-out subset and **31** for the
    partition draw, the last reproducing `e168`'s published figure exactly. So: measure a draw's own effect before
    attributing anything to the manipulation; record a **fingerprint read off what the run actually used**
    (`readout.subset_sha1`, `partition_draw.fingerprint_sha1`, `support_draw.fingerprint_sha1`), never one recomputed
    from the construction; and where a family's claims matter, vary the draw and average rather than quoting one.
    (`docs/findings/2026-09-25-the-interior-fitting-deficit-did-not-replicate.md`,
    `docs/findings/2026-09-25-only-two-of-the-axis-claims-survive-a-second-draw.md`,
    `docs/findings/2026-09-25-more-of-the-corpus-cannot-say-which-draw-it-used-than-can.md`)




## Related work to differentiate against

Four papers are close enough to require explicit positioning — all use fly
*biology* to inspire a learning rule, none uses a connectome-constrained network
as a CL substrate:

- Shen, Dasgupta & Navlakha, *Neural Computation* 35(11):1797, 2023 — associative
  learning in the fly olfactory circuit reduces forgetting.
- Robinson et al., bioRxiv 2023, doi:10.1101/2023.01.18.524467 — long-term memory
  formation inspires generative replay.
- Norman-Tenazas et al., GECCO 2023, doi:10.1145/3589737.3605985 — local learning
  for replay with a recurrent model of the insect memory centre.
- Max, Shen et al., *Neuromorphic Computing and Engineering*, 2026,
  doi:10.1088/2634-4386/ae9177 — few-shot continual learning for spiking
  neuromorphic olfaction.

Crowded areas to avoid claiming novelty in: SNN continual learning by
